verdict.rationale: Docs scatter some security-relevant facts — a submission/review process for third-party plugins (docs-31, docs-40), the scope of data shared via 'Sign in with ChatGPT' (docs-19, docs-23), and examples of what plugins can execute (e.g., reading/sending iMessage, docs-5) — but there is no single, dedicated security-posture document covering telemetry/data collection practices, sandboxing, or a formal trust model for third-party skills. Community comments (codex-plugins-comm-1, comm-6) reflect skepticism that textual skill instructions provide real safety guarantees, but this is general concern rather than a concrete contradiction of a specific documented claim, so it lowers confidence rather than flipping to disputed. Missing for 10: a consolidated security/trust-model page, explicit telemetry/data-collection disclosure, and sandboxing/permission details for third-party skills.
